preFixRegression.c1: Active semantic cancellation did not promptly abort the exact running invocation signal before the executor barrier released.
preFixRegression.c2: Cancellation committed while the attempt_started checkpoint was blocked could still allow one executor invocation after the checkpoint returned.
preFixRegression.c3: Checkpoint acknowledgement could persist revision 2 while the semantic cancellation revision had advanced to revision 5.
preFixRegression.c4: The production source deleted the running entry before awaited settlement/cleanup, so semantic completion could release the physical runtime slot too early; the behavioral capacity floor was retained as an additional falsifier.

implementedRepair.committedEventObservation: CaseEngine publishes only successful committed Events as asynchronous non-authoritative wake hints; observer throw/reject/hang cannot change a semantic mutation and rolled-back mutations publish nothing.
implementedRepair.liveControlIdentity: caseId + taskId + attemptId + fencingToken + executorId + executorEpoch; local controller object identity is used only for exact unregister comparison.
implementedRepair.handshakeOrder: Attempt start -> durable attempt_started checkpoint drain -> authoritative Attempt reread -> controller/live binding creation -> pre-publication reread -> live-control publication -> post-publication reread -> execution-gate release.
implementedRepair.checkpointDrain: Each checkpoint persists the exact snapshot caseRevision, acknowledges exactly that revision, and loops if semantic state advanced during I/O.
implementedRepair.capacityCleanup: Outcome settlement and its checkpoint complete before compare-delete of the running entry, retaining physical capacity through predecessor cleanup.
